Exact Two-Group Contrasts for a Registry of Patient Endpoints

Source: R/analysis-contrasts.R
ContrastPatientEndpoints.Rd

Runs ExactPatientTests() for every row of a hypothesis registry (endpoint, contrast, family) on a wide patient table (one row per patient, one column per endpoint). Contrast arms are declared as sets of patient groups. Two missingness policies are offered:

Usage

ContrastPatientEndpoints(
  data,
  registry,
  contrasts,
  id,
  group,
  endpoint = "endpoint",
  contrast = "contrast",
  family = "family",
  missingness = c("complete_case", "require_complete"),
  hypothesis_prefix = "h",
  max_allocations = 1000000L
)

Arguments

data

Wide patient table with the id, group and endpoint columns.

registry

Data frame with one row per hypothesis and the endpoint, contrast and family columns. Extra columns are ignored.

contrasts

Named list: contrast name to a list with character vectors A and B of patient groups (disjoint).

id, group

Patient identifier and patient group columns of data.

endpoint, contrast, family

Column names in registry.

missingness

"complete_case" or "require_complete".

hypothesis_prefix

Prefix of the generated hypothesis_id (followed by the registry row number).

max_allocations

Passed to ExactPatientTests().

Value

A data frame with the registry columns, hypothesis_id, family_id (family :: contrast), expected and evaluable arm sizes, mean_difference, p_value, allocations, status and missingness, in registry order. Pass it to AdjustPatientFamilies().

Details

  • "complete_case": each hypothesis uses only patients with a finite value; a hypothesis whose arm has no such patient is unavailable. This reproduces tables that silently drop missing patients.

  • "require_complete": every patient of both arms must have a finite value, otherwise the hypothesis is unavailable (no patient is dropped).

Each hypothesis receives its own design, so a registry may repeat an endpoint-contrast pair in different families. The effect is the mean of arm A minus the mean of arm B.

Examples

d <- data.frame(patient = paste0("p", 1:6), arm = rep(c("x", "y"), each = 3),
                e1 = c(1, 2, 3, 6, 7, NA), e2 = c(5, 4, 6, 1, 2, 3))
reg <- data.frame(endpoint = c("e1", "e2"), contrast = "x vs y", family = "f")
ctr <- list("x vs y" = list(A = "x", B = "y"))
ContrastPatientEndpoints(d, reg, ctr, "patient", "arm")
#>   endpoint contrast family hypothesis_id   family_id n_a_expected n_b_expected
#> 1       e1   x vs y      f            h1 f :: x vs y            3            3
#> 2       e2   x vs y      f            h2 f :: x vs y            3            3
#>   n_a_evaluable n_b_evaluable mean_difference p_value allocations status
#> 1             3             2            -4.5     0.1          10  EXACT
#> 2             3             3             3.0     0.1          20  EXACT
#>     missingness
#> 1 complete_case
#> 2 complete_case
ContrastPatientEndpoints(d, reg, ctr, "patient", "arm",
                         missingness = "require_complete")
#>   endpoint contrast family hypothesis_id   family_id n_a_expected n_b_expected
#> 1       e1   x vs y      f            h1 f :: x vs y            3            3
#> 2       e2   x vs y      f            h2 f :: x vs y            3            3
#>   n_a_evaluable n_b_evaluable mean_difference p_value allocations
#> 1             3             2              NA      NA          20
#> 2             3             3               3     0.1          20
#>                   status      missingness
#> 1 UNAVAILABLE_INCOMPLETE require_complete
#> 2                  EXACT require_complete
